newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korean Air Lines cancels night flights to Guam.
newsitem.headline: Korean Air Lines cancels night flights to Guam.

text.p: Korean Air Lines (KAL) said on Sunday it was cancelling its night flights to Guam after a fatal crash of on the Pacific island that killed 226 people, mostly South Koreans, earlier this month.
Flight 801 was regularly scheduled to leave Seoul at 8:10 p.m.(1110 GMT) and arrive in Guam at the pitch dark hour of 1:25 a.m. (1525 GMT), said a spokesman for KAL.

He said the night flights would be replaced with flights leaving Seoul at 9:50 a.m. (0050 GMT) arriving in Guam at 3 p.m. (0500 GMT), and the return flights from Guam to Seoul would also depart the island at 4 p.m. (0600 GMT), before sunset.
The new schedule would be implemented on Monday, making Sunday's overnight flight the last, he said.

KAL 801, a Boeing 747 carrying 254 people, ploughed into a hillside minutes from the Guam airport killing all but 28. The cause of the accident is still under investigation by the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB).

"The schedule has been changed as the construction and transportation ministry determined conditions at night at the Guam airport undesirable and asked that the flights be changed," the spokesman told Reuters by phone.
Separately, the remains of eight bodies from the crash were airlifted to Seoul on Sunday. So far 31 remains have been returned to the families, the spokesman said.
